questions.question: Lalit deposits ₹42,000 in his account that pays an annual interest rate of 20% compounded half yearly. Calculate the total amount in his account after one year.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate is halved (10%) and the time is doubled (2 periods).

Effective rate for 2 successive cycles of 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

**Total Amount** = 121% of 42,000.

⇒ 42,000 × 1.21 = 50,820.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,820.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67e658ea3048af970d2b1de1d8dcd71be9529c1ebbea4018038253e6b61475ef.png] 

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹42,000**

Annual Rate (R) = **20%**

Time (T) = **1 year**

Since the interest is **compounded half yearly**:

⇒ Adjusted Rate (r) = R ÷ 2 = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half year

⇒ Number of periods (n) = T × 2 = 1 × 2 = 2

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 42,000 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 42,000 × (110/100) × (110/100)

⇒ A = 42,000 × 1.1 × 1.1

⇒ A = 42,000 × 1.21

⇒ A = 50,820

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,820.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Half-Yearly Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the **annual rate** is divided by 2 and the **time (in years)** is multiplied by 2 to get the effective number of conversion periods.

Quarterly Compounding

For quarterly compounding, the rate is divided by 4 and the time is multiplied by 4. The formula becomes A = P(1 + R/400)⁴T.

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is an application of successive percentage change. For two periods with rate r, the effective rate is (r + r + r²/100)%.

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 14 min, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 63 min. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in min) will it take to fill one-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net rate of filling = (1/14 − 1/63) = (9 − 2) / 126 = 7 / 126 = 1/18 tank/min.

Time to fill the **full tank** = 18 min.

Time to fill **1/3rd** of the tank = 18 × 1/3 = 6 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Pipe A** (Filling) = 14 min

Time taken by **Pipe B** (Emptying) = 63 min

Let the **Total Capacity** of the tank be the **LCM** of 14 and 63.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work (units)**
 **Efficiency (units/min)**
 
 

 Pipe A (Fill)
 14
 126
 126 ÷ 14 = 9
 
 

 Pipe B (Empty)
 63
 126 ÷ 63 = −2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 9 − 2 = 7 units/min

⇒ Work to be completed = 1/3 × **Total Capacity**

⇒ Work = 1/3 × 126 = 42 units

⇒ Time taken = **Work** ÷ **Efficiency**

⇒ Time taken = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 min

**∴ The correct answer is 6 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (leakage) have **negative efficiency**. Net work is the algebraic sum of efficiencies.

Time-Work Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. If work is constant, Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken.

Fractional Work

To find the time for a fraction of work, multiply the **Total Time** taken for full work by that **fraction**.

questions.question: A number when increased by 110%, gives 3570. The number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Consider the **original number** as 100%.

An **increase of 110%** makes the final percentage = 100% + 110% = 210%.

Given: 210% → 3570

Dividing by 210, we get 1% → 3570 ÷ 210 = 17.

**Original number** (100%) → 17 × 100 = 1700.

**∴ The correct answer is 1700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase = 110%

Resulting value = 3570

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Original Value × (1 + Percentage Increase / 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d9e77d33aba9f732d6e75440ea27be1784527879501cfbb22bb33c3db211020.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original number be **x**.

⇒ x + (110 / 100) × x = 3570

⇒ x + 1.1x = 3570

⇒ 2.1x = 3570

⇒ x = 3570 / 2.1

⇒ x = 35700 / 21

⇒ x = 1700

**∴ The correct answer is 1700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

New Value = Original Value × (100 + Increase%) ÷ 100. This is the standard method for **growth calculations**.

Reverse Percentage

To find the original value when the increased value is known, divide the final value by the **multiplying factor** (e.g., 2.1 for 110% increase).

Fractional Equivalence

An increase of 110% is equivalent to multiplying the number by 21/10 or 2.1. This helps in **fast mental math**.

questions.question: If the fourth proportional to 2x, 3x, and 12 is y, find y.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the first two terms **2x : 3x** simplifies to **2 : 3**.

For **proportion**, the ratio of the next two terms **12 : y** must also be **2 : 3**.

Comparing the parts: **2 units = 12** ⇒ **1 unit = 6**.

Therefore, **y = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18**.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The terms are **2x**, **3x**, **12**, and **y** is the **fourth proportional**.

**Formula Used:** If **a, b, c, d** are in **proportion**, then **a/b = c/d**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff08aba64d3ca096d0117f7dda9cd626789875492ccb9072e31e4938e534dbeb.png] 

⇒ 2x ÷ 3x = 12 ÷ y

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 = 12 ÷ y

⇒ 2 × y = 12 × 3

⇒ 2y = 36

⇒ y = 36 ÷ 2

⇒ y = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in continued proportion, then **a/b = b/c**, where **c = b² ÷ a** is the third proportional.

Product Rule

In any proportion **a : b :: c : d**, the **product of extremes (a × d)** is always equal to the **product of means (b × c)**.

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

43, 44, 43, 53, 42, 44, 46, 47, 55, 50, 52, 55, 40, 45, 44, 53, 48, 48
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Mode** of a data set is the value that appears most **frequently**.

By scanning the given numbers: **44** appears 3 times (at positions 2, 6, and 15).

Other frequent values like 43, 53, 55, and 48 appear only 2 times each.

Since 44 has the highest count, it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {43, 44, 43, 53, 42, 44, 46, 47, 55, 50, 52, 55, 40, 45, 44, 53, 48, 48}

**Formula Used:** Mode = The observation with the **Maximum Frequency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5e8c24f88b279dc0ee1773bdd4b7c129477b4aebb18baed5e8b601e4de7da36.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Count of 40 = 1

⇒ Count of 42 = 1

⇒ Count of 43 = 2

⇒ Count of 44 = 3

⇒ Count of 45 = 1

⇒ Count of 46 = 1

⇒ Count of 47 = 1

⇒ Count of 48 = 2

⇒ Count of 50 = 1

⇒ Count of 52 = 1

⇒ Count of 53 = 2

⇒ Count of 55 = 2

⇒ The maximum frequency is 3, which corresponds to the value **44**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

It is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations: Mean = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n.

Median

The **middle value** of the data when arranged in ascending or descending order. For n = 18 (even), it is the average of the 9th and 10th terms.

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately asymmetrical distribution, the relationship is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Range

The difference between the **maximum** and **minimum** values in the data set: Range = Max − Min.

questions.question: A trader claims to sell spice at a profit of 15% but also dishonestly uses a weight which is 14% less than what is mentioned on it. Find the total percentage of profit earned by the trader. (Round the answer to the nearest whole number)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Profit Percentage** = [ (100 + **Profit%**) / (100 − **Less Weight%**) − 1 ] × 100

Total Profit % = [ (100 + 15) / (100 − 14) − 1 ] × 100

Total Profit % = [ 115 / 86 − 1 ] × 100 = (29 / 86) × 100

Total Profit % ≈ 33.72%

Rounding to the **nearest whole number**, we get 34%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Claimed **Profit** = 15%

Dishonest **Weight reduction** = 14%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4fe9a0f90f74f16a10d497c480ca6944be1276096b975e31c7d3439c849056e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1000g spice be ₹1000.

⇒ Trader sells at 15% profit, so **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 + 15% of 1000 = ₹1150.

⇒ Trader uses 14% less weight, so **Actual weight** given = 1000 − 14% of 1000 = 860g.

⇒ **Cost Price** for the trader for 860g = ₹860.

⇒ Total **Profit** = SP − Actual CP = 1150 − 860 = ₹290.

⇒ Total **Profit %** = (Profit / Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Total Profit % = (290 / 860) × 100 = 2900 / 86 ≈ 33.7209%.

⇒ Rounding to the nearest whole number → 34%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % = [ (True Weight − Faulty Weight) / Faulty Weight ] × 100. When both profit margin and faulty weight are involved, use the ratio of multipliers.

Successive Percentage for Profit

Total Gain % = [ (1 + g₁/100)(1 + g₂/100) − 1 ] × 100, where g₁ is the price gain and g₂ is the gain from weight manipulation.

Effective Weight Gain

If a trader cheats by x% while buying and y% while selling using faulty weights, the net profit is calculated based on the actual quantity handled relative to the stated price.

questions.question: If the product of two numbers is 98,304 and their HCF is 128, then find the LCM of the numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Formula: **LCM = Product ÷ HCF**

Substitute the values: **LCM = 98,304 ÷ 128**

Shortcut (Unit Digit Method): The unit digit of the product is 4 and the HCF is 8. Since 8 × 8 = 64, the unit digit of the **LCM** must be 8.

Checking options: Only 768 ends with 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of **two numbers** = 98,304

**HCF** (Highest Common Factor) = 128

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = **HCF × LCM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d020489486c8e0464f151ca3fe04bc1a2e548ea59b8b94b508a6b053d2cf939.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 98,304 = 128 × **LCM**

⇒ LCM = 98,304 ÷ 128

⇒ LCM = 768

**∴ The correct answer is 768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any **two numbers** x and y, their Product = HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y). This specific identity does not hold true for three or more numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

LCM of Fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators). HCF of Fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

Divisibility Rule

The **LCM** of any set of numbers is always exactly divisible by the **HCF** of that same set of numbers.

questions.question: If 9A7B is divisible by 55, find A + B.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ A number is **divisible by 55** if it is divisible by both **5 and 11**. questions.question: The difference between the present ages of Ayushi and Nidhi is 21 years. Five years ago from now, the sum of their ages was 83 years. If Ayushi is older than Nidhi, find Nidhi's present age (in years).

questions.question: A 180-meter-long train passes a pole in 12 seconds. A second 120-meter-long train is moving in the same direction as of the first train and crosses the first train in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** of first train = 180 / 12 = 15 m/s.

**Relative Speed** = (Total Length) ÷ Time = (180 + 120) / 15 = 300 / 15 = 20 m/s.

In **same direction**, Relative Speed = Speed₂ − Speed₁.

Speed of second train = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s.

Convert to **km/h**: 35 × (18/5) = 126 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 126 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 180 m

Time to pass a **stationary pole** = 12 sec

Length of second train (L₂) = 120 m

Time to cross each other in **same direction** = 15 sec

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11f4958787cac0b5134031a0a7a3401aee8bf2cd8012223fa8176ef381c35d61.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of first train (v₁) = Length / Time

⇒ v₁ = 180 / 12 = 15 m/s

⇒ Total distance covered during crossing = L₁ + L₂

⇒ Total Distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m

⇒ Relative Speed (v₂ − v₁) = Total Distance / Time of crossing

⇒ v₂ − 15 = 300 / 15

⇒ v₂ − 15 = 20

⇒ v₂ = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

⇒ Speed of second train in **km/h** = 35 × (18/5)

⇒ Speed = 7 × 18 = 126 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 126 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). If they move in **opposite directions**, it is the **sum** (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5. To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains, regardless of the direction of motion.

questions.question: Simplify: ((120 - 12) div (24 div 2) - 12 + 7)/(5 times 12 div 10 - (6 times 4) div 12)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **Numerator** and **Denominator** independently using the **BODMAS rule**.

**Numerator**: (108 ÷ 12) − 12 + 7 ⇒ 9 − 12 + 7 = 4

**Denominator**: (60 ÷ 10) − (24 ÷ 12) ⇒ 6 − 2 = 4

Simplified result = 4 ÷ 4 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: ((120 − 12) ÷ (24 ÷ 2) − 12 + 7) / (5 × 12 ÷ 10 − (6 × 4) ÷ 12)

**Formula Used:**

The **BODMAS rule** defines the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = (120 − 12) ÷ (24 ÷ 2) − 12 + 7

⇒ Numerator = 108 ÷ 12 − 12 + 7

⇒ Numerator = 9 − 12 + 7 = 4

⇒ Denominator = (5 × 12 ÷ 10) − (6 × 4 ÷ 12)

⇒ Denominator = (60 ÷ 10) − (24 ÷ 12)

⇒ Denominator = 6 − 2 = 4

⇒ Final Expression = 4 / 4 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always solve **Brackets** first (round (), then curly {}, then square []), followed by **Division** and **Multiplication** (from left to right), and finally **Addition** and **Subtraction**.

Fraction Simplification

When simplifying complex fractions, treat the **Numerator** and **Denominator** as separate expressions and simplify them completely before performing the final division.

Operator Precedence

Multiplication and division hold the same level of precedence; if both appear, solve the expression starting from the **left side** to the **right side**.

questions.question: If the area of an equilateral triangle is given as 900 m², then what is its perimeter?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of an equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × **side**² ⇒ 900 = (√3/4) × a².

**side** (a) = √(3600 / √3) = 60 / 3¹/⁴.

**Perimeter** = 3 × **side** = 3 × (60 / 3¹/⁴) = 60 × 3¹ − ¹/⁴ = 60 × 3³/⁴.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by both 6 and 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number **divisible** by both 6 and 9 must be a multiple of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

**LCM** of 6 and 9 ⇒ 18.

Check the given options for multiples of 18: 18, 36, **54**, **72**, **90**...

45 is not a multiple of 18 as 18 × 2.5 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

To be **divisible by both 6 and 9**, a number must be **even** (divisible by 2), its sum of digits must be divisible by 3 (for 6), and its sum of digits must be divisible by 9.

**Given Numbers:** 54, 45, 90, 72

**Step 1: Check Divisibility by 6 (Divisible by 2 and 3)**

⇒ 54: Ends in 4 (Even) and 5 + 4 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

⇒ 45: Ends in 5 (Odd) → **NOT divisible by 6**.

⇒ 90: Ends in 0 (Even) and 9 + 0 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

⇒ 72: Ends in 2 (Even) and 7 + 2 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

**Step 2: Check Divisibility by 9 (Sum of digits divisible by 9)**

⇒ 54: 5 + 4 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 45: 4 + 5 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 90: 9 + 0 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 72: 7 + 2 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

Since 45 is divisible by 9 but **NOT** by 6, it is the correct choice.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is simultaneously divisible by both **2** (last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8) and **3** (sum of digits is a multiple of 3).

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is completely divisible by 9.

LCM Method for Combined Divisibility

To check divisibility by multiple numbers, find the **LCM** of those numbers; any common multiple must be divisible by this LCM.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 13 and ab + bc + ca = 4, then what is the value of ab(a + b) + bc(b + c) + ca(c + a) + 3abc?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **c = 0** as there are 3 variables and only 2 equations.

From the given: **a + b = 13** and **ab = 4**.

The expression reduces to **ab(a + b) + 0 + 0 + 0**.

Substituting the values: **4 × 13 = 52**.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **a + b + c = 13** and **ab + bc + ca = 4**.

From **a + b + c = 13**, we can derive:

⇒ **a + b = 13 − c**

⇒ **b + c = 13 − a**

⇒ **c + a = 13 − b**

Now, substitute these into the required expression **ab(a + b) + bc(b + c) + ca(c + a) + 3abc**:

⇒ ab(**13 − c**) + bc(**13 − a**) + ca(**13 − b**) + 3abc

⇒ 13ab − abc + 13bc − abc + 13ca − abc + 3abc

⇒ 13(ab + bc + ca) − 3abc + 3abc

⇒ 13(**4**)

⇒ **52**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Trinomial

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). This identity relates the sum of terms, sum of squares, and sum of products taken two at a time.

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

In competitive exams, if an expression is symmetric and there are more variables than equations, setting one variable to **0** or **1** often leads to a quick solution.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like the Normal Distribution), the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positively Skewed Distribution

In a **positively skewed** (right-skewed) distribution, the values generally follow the order: **Mean > Median > Mode**.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

Karl Pearson Formula

questions.question: The difference between two parallel sides of a trapezium is 9 cm. The perpendicular distance between them is 52 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 988 cm ², find the lengths of the parallel sides (in cm).

**∴ The correct answer is 23.5, 14.5 cm.**

questions.question:
Which of the following are properties of ionic compounds?

A. High melting point

B. Soluble in non-polar solvents

C. Conduct electricity in solid state

D. Brittle in nature
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (A) and (D)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement A refers to **High melting and boiling points**. Ionic compounds are composed of a giant **3D crystal lattice** where ions are held together by exceptionally strong **electrostatic forces** of attraction. Overcoming these forces to change the state requires a massive amount of **thermal energy**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• Statement B discusses solubility in **non-polar solvents**. Ionic compounds are **polar** and strictly follow the **like dissolves like** principle. While they dissolve readily in **polar solvents** like **water** (due to ion-dipole interactions), they are generally insoluble in **non-polar solvents** such as **benzene**, **ether**, or **kerosene**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• Statement C describes **electrical conductivity** in the solid state. In solid form, the ions are locked in fixed positions within the **crystalline structure** and are not free to move. Electricity is only conducted in **molten** or **aqueous** states where the **lattice** breaks down, allowing ions to migrate. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• Statement D highlights that these compounds are **brittle**. When a mechanical force is applied, layers of the **lattice** shift, bringing ions of the **same charge** into close proximity. The resulting **strong electrostatic repulsion** causes the crystal to shatter easily. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Ionic Bonding**:

 
 
• Formed through the **complete transfer** of valence electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
 
• Involves the formation of **cations** (positive) and **anions** (negative).
 
• Prominent examples include **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** and **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)**.
 
 
 
• **Solubility and Hydration**:
 
 
• Solubility depends on the balance between **Lattice Energy** and **Hydration Energy**.
 
• **Water** has a high **dielectric constant**, which effectively weakens the attraction between ions, facilitating dissolution.
 
 
 
• **Crystalline Structure**:
 
 
• Ionic solids exist as **regular geometric patterns** rather than discrete molecules.
 
• The specific **coordination number** of an ion depends on the relative sizes of the **cation** and **anion**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true when a beam of white light is incident on a glass prism?

(i) The white light undergoes dispersion.

(ii) The speed of light remains constant when it goes from air into the prism.

(iii) The speed of light decreases as the light goes from air into the prism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (i) refers to the phenomenon where **white light**, upon entering a **glass prism**, splits into its constituent spectrum of seven colors. This occurs because different colors of light possess different **wavelengths** and travel at different speeds within the glass, causing them to bend at different angles. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• Statement (ii) claims that the speed of light remains constant. In physics, the speed of light is only a constant (approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s) in a **vacuum**. When light transitions from a rarer medium like **air** to a denser medium like **glass**, its velocity must change according to the optical density of the material. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (iii) correctly identifies that the speed of light decreases. **Glass** has a higher **refractive index** (approximately 1.5) compared to air (approximately 1.0003). As per the relation **v = c/n**, where **v** is the velocity in the medium and **n** is the refractive index, a higher index leads to a lower velocity. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction and Dispersion:**

 
 
• **Refraction** is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent substance into another. This bending is caused by the **change in speed**.
 
• The **Angle of Deviation** depends on the wavelength; **Violet light** deviates the most because it has the shortest wavelength and slows down the most, while **Red light** deviates the least.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index (n):**
 
 
• It is a dimensionless number that describes how fast light travels through the material.
 
• The **Absolute Refractive Index** is calculated as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** to the **speed of light in the medium**.
 
• For **optical glass**, the index typically ranges from 1.5 to 1.9 depending on the density and composition.

• Calculation: **40 × (5/18) = 200 / 18**.
 
• Performing the division: **200 ÷ 18 = 11.111...**, which is rounded to **11.11 m/s**.

__
 
• **Average velocity** is defined as the total **displacement** divided by the **total time** taken for the motion.
 
• **Displacement** is a **vector quantity** that measures the shortest straight-line distance between the **initial position** and the **final position** of an object.
 
• In this problem, Reshma swims in a **120 m** long pool and covers a total distance of **240 m**. This indicates she swims from the starting point to the other end (**120 m**) and returns to the **original starting point** (another **120 m**).
 
• Because she returns to her **starting position**, her final position is the same as her initial position. Therefore, her total **displacement is 0 m**.
 
• The time taken is given as **1 minute**, which is equal to **60 seconds**.
 
• Calculating the **average velocity** using the formula: Average Velocity = Total Displacement / Total Time = 0 m / 60 s = **0 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• In this scenario, the **total distance** is **240 m**.
 
• The average speed would be 240 m / 60 s = **4 m/s**.

• **Distance** and **speed** are **scalar quantities** as they only have magnitude.

questions.question: Why are xylem and phloem called “complex permanent tissues”?

• **Xylem** and **phloem** are the primary **conducting tissues** or **vascular tissues** in plants, acting as a plumbing system for nutrient and water movement.

• **Constituents of Phloem**:

• It is primarily used in **water treatment** and does not involve movement across membranes based on concentration.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**
 
 
• A **phase transition** where molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to enter the gaseous state.
 
• While it can change liquid levels, it is not driven by **solute gradients** or **membrane filtration**.

• **Fleming’s Left Hand Rule** is a fundamental principle used in **electromagnetism** to find the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• The **First finger** (also known as the **Index finger** or **Forefinger**) represents the direction of the **Magnetic Field**, typically directed from the **North Pole** to the **South Pole**.
 
• The **Middle finger** represents the direction of the **Electric Current** flowing through the wire (from positive to negative terminal).

questions.question: What is the main purpose of hybridisation in crop improvement programmes?

options.text: To grow crops without using fertilizers or irrigation
To increase the natural mutation rate in crop plants

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Hybridisation** is a fundamental technique in **crop improvement** that involves the crossing of two or more plants with different **genetic makeups** to produce a progeny called a **hybrid**.
 
• The primary objective of this process is to aggregate **superior traits** from different parents—such as **high yield**, **disease resistance**, **early maturity**, and **nutritional quality**—into a single **genotype**.
 
• It utilizes the concept of **genetic recombination**, where the reshuffling of genes during **meiosis** and subsequent fertilization creates **genotypic variations** that do not exist in the original parental lines.
 
• Hybridisation often leads to **Heterosis**, also known as **hybrid vigor**, where the offspring exhibits enhanced physiological characteristics and **biological efficiency** compared to either parent.
 
• The process typically involves careful **selection of parents**, **emasculation** (removal of anthers), and controlled **pollination** to ensure the desired genetic transfer occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mutation Breeding**:

 
 
• Unlike hybridisation, this method uses **mutagens** (like **Gamma rays** or chemicals) to induce sudden, inheritable changes in the DNA sequence to create new traits.
 
 
 
• **Cloning and Micropropagation**:
 
 
• This involves **asexual reproduction** to produce **Somaclones**. These plants are genetically identical to the parent, which is the opposite of the genetic diversity aimed for in hybridisation.
 
 
 
• **Types of Hybridisation**:
 
 
• **Inter-varietal**: Cross between two different varieties of the same species.
 
• **Inter-specific**: Cross between two different species of the same genus.
 
• **Inter-generic**: Cross between plants belonging to two different genera, often used to introduce **hardiness** or **stress tolerance**.

the atom is mostly empty space

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1911**, **Ernest Rutherford** conducted the **alpha-particle scattering experiment** by bombarding a very thin **gold foil** (approximately 1000 atoms thick) with high-energy **alpha particles**. Hence, the observation that most particles passed **straight through** the foil was central to his atomic model.
 
• The observation that a **vast majority** (nearly 99%) of the **alpha particles** traveled through the gold foil without any **deflection** or change in direction led to the conclusion that the **atom is mostly empty space**. ***Hence, the statement that the atom is mostly empty space is correct.***
 
• Since these **positively charged** helium ions did not encounter any **electrostatic repulsion** or physical obstruction in their path, it indicated that the **mass** and **positive charge** of the atom were not spread out as previously suggested by the **Plum Pudding Model**. ***Hence, the conclusion regarding the empty nature of the atom is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rutherford's Atomic Model** provided several other groundbreaking insights:

 
 
• **The Nucleus**: A very small fraction of particles were deflected by large angles, and 1 in 12,000 rebounded completely (180°), proving that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** are concentrated in a tiny region called the **nucleus**.
 
• **Nuclear Charge**: Because alpha particles (He²⁺) are positive, their deflection by the center confirmed that the **nucleus is positively charged**, not negatively charged.
 
• **Size Proportions**: Rutherford estimated that the radius of the **nucleus** is about 10⁵ times smaller than the radius of the **atom**, reinforcing the **empty space** theory.
 
• **Electron Orbits**: The model proposed that **electrons** revolve around the nucleus in circular paths, similar to planets revolving around the sun.

questions.question: If the radius of the Earth were to double while mass remains the same, the new value of g would be ___________the original value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on the surface of a planet is calculated using the formula g = GM/R², where G represents the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, M is the **mass of the planet**, and R is its **radius**.
 
• According to the question, the **mass (M)** of the Earth remains constant while the **radius (R)** is doubled, such that the new radius R' = 2R.
 
• By substituting the new radius into the gravitational formula, the new acceleration g' is expressed as g' = GM / (2R)². Squaring the term in the denominator results in g' = GM / 4R².
 
• Comparing the new equation to the original formula (g = GM/R²) shows that the new gravity g' is equal to (1/4) × g. This mathematically confirms that the gravitational pull becomes **one-fourth** of the original value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:

 
 
• First measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798, its value is approximately 6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg². It is a **scalar quantity** and remains uniform throughout the universe.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting 'g'**:
 
 
• **Shape of the Earth**: Earth is an **oblate spheroid**; the radius at the **equator** is about 21 km longer than at the **poles**. Consequently, g is **maximum at the poles** and **minimum at the equator**.
 
• **Altitude and Depth**: The value of g decreases as we move **upwards** from the surface (altitude) or **downwards** into the Earth (depth). At the **center of the Earth**, the value of g becomes zero.
 
• **Rotation**: The **centrifugal force** generated by Earth's rotation reduces the effective value of g, specifically at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Inverse Square Law**: Gravity follows an **inverse square relationship** with distance. If the distance from the center of mass doubles, the force of attraction is reduced to 2² or 4 times less.

questions.question: If a conductor has a potential difference of 1 V across its ends and a current of 1 A flows through it, what is the resistance of the conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law**, formulated by the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, defines the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
• The law states that the **electric current (I)** flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **potential difference (V)** across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical formula for this relationship is **V = I × R**, which can be rearranged to find **resistance (R)** using **R = V ÷ I**.
 
• In this problem, the **potential difference (V)** is given as **1 Volt (1 V)** and the **current (I)** is given as **1 Ampere (1 A)**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **R = 1 V ÷ 1 A = 1 Ω**.
 
• Thus, the **electrical resistance** of the conductor is exactly **1 Ω**, indicating that for every volt of potential applied, one ampere of current will flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Resistance (R)**:

 
 
• **Definition**: It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of **electric charges** (electrons).
 
• **SI Unit**: The unit of resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**. One ohm is defined as the resistance of a conductor such that a potential difference of **1 Volt** causes a current of **1 Ampere** to flow.
 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**: While resistance depends on shape and size, **resistivity** is an intrinsic property of the material. Metals like **Silver** and **Copper** have very low resistivity.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**:
 
 
• **Length (L)**: Resistance is directly proportional to the **length** of the conductor. Doubling the length doubles the resistance.
 
• **Cross-sectional Area (A)**: Resistance is inversely proportional to the **area**. A thicker wire has less resistance than a thinner wire of the same material.
 
• **Temperature**: In metallic conductors, resistance increases with an increase in **temperature** due to more frequent collisions between electrons and metal ions.

questions.question: A body of mass 10 kg is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 10 m/s. How much potential energy will be possessed by the body when it reaches the maximum height? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem is based on the **Law of Conservation of Mechanical Energy**, which states that the total mechanical energy (sum of kinetic and potential energy) of an object remains constant if only conservative forces like **gravity** are acting on it.
 
• The **mass** (m) of the body is given as **10 kg** and the initial **velocity** (u) with which it is thrown upwards is **10 m/s**.
 
• At the moment of projection (ground level), the body possesses maximum **Kinetic Energy** (KE) and zero **Potential Energy** (PE). The formula for Kinetic Energy is KE = (1)/(2)mv² .
 
• By substituting the given values, the initial Kinetic Energy is calculated as: 1/2 × 10 kg × (10 m/s)² = 1/2 × 10 × 100 = **500 Joules**.
 
• As the body rises, its velocity decreases due to the **acceleration due to gravity** (g = 10 m/s²), and its Kinetic Energy is converted into **Gravitational Potential Energy**.
 
• At the **maximum height**, the vertical velocity of the body becomes zero, meaning its Kinetic Energy becomes **0 J**.
 
• According to the conservation principle, the entire initial Kinetic Energy (500 J) must be converted into Potential Energy at this peak point. Hence, the Potential Energy at maximum height is **500 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE) formula**:

 
 
• Potential energy can also be calculated using the formula **PE = mgh**, where **h** is the height above the reference level.
 
• Using the kinematic equation v² = u² − 2gh, and setting final velocity v = 0 at maximum height: 0 = 10² − 2 × 10 × h, which results in **h = 5 meters**.
 
• Placing this height back into the PE formula: 10 kg × 10 m/s² × 5 m = **500 J**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Measurements**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule** (J), named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• One Joule is defined as the work done by a force of one **Newton** acting through a distance of one **meter**.
 
• In terms of base units, 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².

questions.question: Food chains generally do not extend beyond four trophic levels because:

options.text: of large loss of energy at each level

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**of large loss of energy at each level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The length of a **food chain** is primarily limited by the efficiency of **energy transfer** between different **trophic levels** in an **ecosystem**.
 
• According to the **Ten Percent Law**, formulated by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, only about **10%** of the energy stored as **organic matter** in one trophic level is passed on to the next.
 
• The remaining **90%** of energy is lost to the environment as **heat** during **respiration**, or consumed during **metabolic activities** like growth, movement, and reproduction.
 
• As a result, the amount of available energy decreases exponentially as one moves up the **trophic hierarchy** (from **producers** to **primary consumers**, then **secondary consumers**, and so on).
 
• By the time the energy reaches the **fourth or fifth trophic level**, the residual energy is insufficient to support a stable population of higher-level **predators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**:

 
 
• **First Level (Producers)**: Includes **autotrophs** like green plants and **phytoplankton** that convert **solar energy** into chemical energy via **photosynthesis**.
 
• **Second Level (Primary Consumers)**: Comprises **herbivores** that feed directly on producers.
 
• **Third and Fourth Levels (Secondary/Tertiary Consumers)**: Consists of **carnivores** and **apex predators**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Pyramids**:
 
 
• The **Pyramid of Energy** is always **upright** because energy is lost at every step; it can never be inverted, unlike pyramids of biomass or numbers in specific ecosystems.
 
• **Decomposers**: While **saprotrophs** like fungi and bacteria are essential for **nutrient cycling**, they operate outside the linear sequence of the energy-limited food chain.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why anaerobic respiration releases less energy than aerobic respiration?

options.text: It occurs slower than aerobic respiration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It partially breaks down glucose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerobic respiration** involves the complete oxidation of **glucose** in the presence of **Oxygen** (O₂). This process breaks the carbon-carbon bonds entirely, converting glucose into **Carbon Dioxide** (CO₂) and **Water** (H₂O), releasing a high amount of energy, typically **36 to 38 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
• **Anaerobic respiration** occurs in the absence of **Oxygen**. In this pathway, **glucose** is only **partially broken down** or oxidized. Because the chemical bonds are not fully disrupted, a significant portion of the energy remains trapped within the organic end-products.
 
• In **yeast** and plants, the partial breakdown results in **Ethanol** and **CO₂** (alcoholic fermentation), whereas in **animal muscle cells** during vigorous exercise, it results in **Lactic Acid**.
 
• From a bioenergetic perspective, anaerobic respiration yields a net gain of only **2 ATP** molecules. This energy is derived solely from the **Glycolysis** stage, as the **Krebs Cycle** and **Electron Transport Chain** cannot function without oxygen acting as the final electron acceptor.
 
• The lack of oxygen prevents the full extraction of high-energy electrons from **NADH** through **oxidative phosphorylation**, which is the most efficient stage of energy production in **mitochondria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Enzymatic Dependency**:

 
 
• Both aerobic and anaerobic pathways are highly dependent on **enzymes**. For instance, **Glycolysis** requires enzymes like **Hexokinase**, and anaerobic fermentation requires **Lactate Dehydrogenase** or **Pyruvate Decarboxylase**.
 
 
 
• **Rate of Respiration**:
 
 
• While anaerobic respiration is less efficient in terms of energy yield per molecule, it can proceed at a much **faster rate** than aerobic respiration, providing a quick burst of **ATP** when oxygen levels are depleted.
 
 
 
• **Location of Processes**:
 
 
• Anaerobic respiration occurs entirely within the **Cytoplasm** of the cell. In contrast, aerobic respiration starts in the cytoplasm but completes its high-energy yielding stages within the **Mitochondria**.

questions.question: Ethanol and ethanoic acid react in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form a sweet-smelling compound. Which of the following correctly identifies the reaction type and the role of concentrated H₂SO₄?

options.text: It is a neutralization reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as an acid to neutralize the base.
It is an oxidation reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as an oxidizing agent.
It is an esterification reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent.
It is a substitution reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent to remove water molecules.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is an esterification reaction; H2SO4 acts as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Esterification** is a specific type of organic reaction where a **carboxylic acid** reacts with an **alcohol** to form an **ester** and water as a byproduct.
 
• In the given scenario, **ethanoic acid** (CH₃COOH) reacts with **ethanol** (C₂H₅OH) to produce **ethyl ethanoate** (CH₃COOC₂H₅), a compound famous for its **sweet, fruity fragrance**.
 
• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** (H₂SO₄) plays a dual role in this reaction: it serves as a **Brønsted acid catalyst** by providing protons to activate the carboxylic acid group.
 
• Simultaneously, it acts as a **dehydrating agent**. Since the esterification process is **reversible**, the acid removes the water molecules produced during the reaction.
 
• According to **Le Chatelier's Principle**, the removal of a product (water) shifts the **chemical equilibrium** toward the forward direction, significantly increasing the yield of the ester.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Reactants**:

 
 
• **Ethanol**: A primary alcohol used as a solvent and fuel; it does not behave as a typical inorganic base, so the reaction is not a standard **neutralization**.
 
• **Ethanoic Acid**: Also known as acetic acid, it is a weak organic acid that provides the **acyl group** for the ester.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Reaction Types**:
 
 
• **Neutralization**: This typically involves the reaction between an acid and a base to form an inorganic salt and water (e.g., HCl + NaOH).
 
• **Oxidation**: The oxidation of ethanol using **alkaline KMnO₄** or **acidified K₂Cr₂O₇** would convert it into ethanoic acid, rather than forming an ester.
 
• **Substitution**: While esterification involves an **acyl nucleophilic substitution** mechanism, it is specifically categorized as a **condensation reaction** due to the loss of a small water molecule.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Esters**:
 
 
• Esters are primarily used in the manufacture of **perfumes**, **cosmetics**, and **artificial flavorings**.
 
• They undergo **saponification** when reacted with a base like NaOH to produce **soap** and the original alcohol.

questions.question: What is the formula unit mass of ammonium sulphate (NH₄)₂SO₄?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**132 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is defined as the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms in a **formula unit** of a compound. It is calculated in the same manner as molecular mass, but specifically for substances whose constituent particles are **ions**.
 
• The chemical formula for **Ammonium Sulphate** is **(NH₄)₂SO₄**. It consists of two **Ammonium (NH₄⁺)** ions and one **Sulphate (SO₄²−)** ion.
 
• To determine the mass, the atomic masses of the individual elements are required: **Nitrogen (N)** is **14 u**, **Hydrogen (H)** is **1 u**, **Sulphur (S)** is **32 u**, and **Oxygen (O)** is **16 u**.
 
• Calculation for the **Ammonium** part: The formula **(NH₄)₂** contains 2 atoms of Nitrogen and 8 atoms of Hydrogen. Mass = (2 × 14) + (8 × 1) = 28 + 8 = **36 u**.
 
• Calculation for the **Sulphate** part: The formula **SO₄** contains 1 atom of Sulphur and 4 atoms of Oxygen. Mass = (1 × 32) + (4 × 16) = 32 + 64 = **96 u**.
 
• The total **formula unit mass** is the sum of these components: 36 u + 96 u = **132 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a **colorless** or **white crystalline** salt, often used as a **synthetic fertilizer** for soil.
 
• It is particularly effective in **alkaline soils** as it releases a small amount of **acid**, lowering the **pH** of the soil while contributing essential **Nitrogen** for plant growth.
 
• In addition to agriculture, it is utilized in the **food industry** as an acidity regulator and in **biochemistry** for the purification of **proteins** through the process of **ammonium sulphate precipitation**.
 
• The compound is produced industrially by reacting **ammonia** with **sulphuric acid**.

questions.question: Which policy of Lord Dalhousie was a significant political cause of the 1857 Revolt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doctrine of Lapse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Doctrine of Lapse** was an imperialistic annexation policy implemented by **Lord Dalhousie**, who served as the **Governor-General of India** from **1848 to 1856**.
 
• According to this policy, any Indian princely state under the **suzerainty** of the **British East India Company** would be annexed if the ruler died without a direct natural male heir.
 
• It fundamentally challenged Indian traditions by refusing to recognize **adopted heirs** as legal successors to the throne, which caused intense resentment among the ruling classes.
 
• Major princely states annexed under this doctrine included **Satara (1848)**, **Jaitpur (1849)**, **Sambalpur (1849)**, **Udaipur (1852)**, **Jhansi (1854)**, and **Nagpur (1854)**.
 
• The annexation of **Jhansi** following the death of **Raja Gangadhar Rao** was a direct catalyst for **Rani Lakshmibai** to join the **Revolt of 1857** to reclaim her kingdom.
 
• This policy, combined with the annexation of **Awadh** on grounds of misgovernance in **1856**, created an atmosphere of fear and distrust, serving as a primary **political cause** for the uprising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It divided the administration into **Diwani** (revenue rights) held by the British and **Nizamat** (administrative duties) held by the Nawab.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System**:
 
 
• A land revenue system introduced by **Sir Thomas Munro** and **Alexander Read** in **1820**, primarily in the **Madras** and **Bombay** Presidencies.
 
• It involved a direct settlement between the government and the **ryots** (individual cultivators) without the use of intermediaries like Zamindars.
 
 
 
• **Vernacular Press Act**:
 
 
• Proposed by **Lord Lytton** in **1878** to restrict the freedom of Indian-language newspapers.
 
• It was aimed at preventing the press from criticizing British policies, particularly during the **Second Anglo-Afghan War**.

questions.question: Which of the following committees, in its 2009 report, is known for introducing a widely used method to estimate poverty levels in India?

__
 
• The **Suresh Tendulkar Committee** was constituted by the **Planning Commission** in **2005** to review the methodology for poverty estimation; it submitted its highly influential report in **2009**.
 
• The committee moved away from the traditional **calorie-based poverty estimation** model, which had been the standard since the **Lakdawala Committee**, and shifted toward a **private expenditure** approach based on consumption.
 
• It introduced a more comprehensive **Poverty Line Basket (PLB)** that included essential expenditures on **health** and **education**, marking a significant departure from previous models that focused primarily on food intake.
 
• The committee recommended the use of **Mixed Reference Period (MRP)** based estimates, which utilize a **365-day recall period** for infrequent purchases like clothing and durables, and a **30-day recall period** for food items.
 
• Under this methodology, the poverty line was calculated as a **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure (MPCE)**, determining that **37.2 percent** of the Indian population lived below the poverty line in **2004-05**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Constituted in **2012** to address criticisms of the Tendulkar methodology, it submitted its findings in **2014**.
 
• It suggested a higher poverty line and recommended a modified **calorie-protein-fat** consumption requirement alongside non-food expenses.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Poverty Estimation**:
 
 
• **Alagh Committee (1979)**: First to define a poverty line based on nutritional requirements (**2400 calories** for rural and **2100 calories** for urban areas).
 
• **Lakdawala Committee (1993)**: Introduced state-specific poverty lines based on the **Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** and **Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW)**.
 
• **NITI Aayog**: In **2015**, it replaced the Planning Commission and established a **Task Force on Elimination of Poverty** headed by **Arvind Panagariya** to further refine these metrics.

• **Anandkumar Velkumar** made history by becoming the **first Indian athlete** to clinch a **gold medal** in the **senior category** at the **World Speed Skating Championships**.
 
• He achieved this feat in the **1,000 m sprint** event, held in **September 2025**, marking a paradigm shift for **Indian roller sports** on the international stage.
 
• The **1,000 m sprint** is a high-intensity track race that requires a precise combination of **aerobic endurance**, **anaerobic power**, and tactical maneuvering during the final laps.
 
• Prior to this victory, India had achieved success primarily in the **junior divisions**, making this **senior world title** a landmark achievement for the **Roller Skating Federation of India (RSFI)**.
 
• His performance at the championships reflects the growing infrastructure and professional training standards for **speed skating** within India, particularly in states like **Tamil Nadu** and **Karnataka**.

questions.question: Which of the following Directive Principles was NOT added to the Indian Constitution as part of the 42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976?

options.text: Article 39A: To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor
Article 48A: To protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife
Article 38: State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities
Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 38: State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** was inserted into the **Indian Constitution** by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976**. It directs the State to ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on a basis of **equal opportunity** and provides **free legal aid** to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Article 48A** was added by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976** under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**. This article mandates that the State shall endeavour to protect and improve the **environment** and to safeguard the **forests** and **wildlife** of the country. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **Article 38** originally existed in the Constitution, but its second clause, which requires the State to **minimise inequalities in income** and eliminate inequalities in **status, facilities, and opportunities**, was inserted by the **44th Amendment Act of 1978** during the Morarji Desai-led government. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Article 39** clause (f) was amended by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976**. It emphasizes that children should be given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of **freedom and dignity**, protecting them against **exploitation** and moral and material abandonment. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976)**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **Mini-Constitution** due to its massive scope of changes.
 
• It added three new words to the **Preamble**: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• It introduced **Fundamental Duties** for citizens by adding **Part IV-A** (Article 51A).
 
• It added four new Directive Principles: **Article 39** (f), **Article 39A**, **Article 43A** (Participation of workers in management), and **Article 48A**.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978)**:
 
 
• Enacted to nullify several provisions introduced by the 42ⁿd Amendment during the Emergency.
 
• It removed the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights** and made it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
• It substituted the words 'internal disturbance' with '**armed rebellion**' in respect of **National Emergency** (Article 352).

questions.question: Which of the following successfully conducted user trials of the Akash-NG missile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the flight trial of the **New Generation Akash (Akash-NG)** missile from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, off the coast of **Odisha**.
 
• The **Akash-NG** is a state-of-the-art **Surface-to-Air Missile (SAM)** system specifically designed for the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** to intercept high-speed, agile aerial threats with low radar signatures.
 
• The flight test was conducted against a high-speed unmanned aerial target at a very low altitude, successfully validating the functioning of the complete weapon system, including the **missile**, **indigenous seeker**, and **launcher**.
 
• The missile system features a **dual-pulse solid rocket motor**, which significantly enhances its speed and provides an operational range of approximately **70 to 80 kilometers**.
 
• It is equipped with an **Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)** multi-function radar that provides the capability to track and engage multiple targets from various directions simultaneously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**:

 
 
• A **Navratna Public Sector Undertaking (PSU)** under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• It acts as the lead integrator for the production of **radar systems** and electronic components for the **Akash** missile family.
 
 
 
• **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**:
 
 
• Headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it is a premier aerospace company.
 
• Focuses on the design and manufacture of **fighter jets** like **Tejas**, **helicopters**, and **gas turbine engines**.
 
 
 
• **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited**:
 
 
• Located in **Mumbai**, it is India's leading shipyard.
 
• Specializes in the construction of **destroyers**, **stealth frigates**, and **Scorpene-class submarines** for the **Indian Navy**.
